What is an access control list (ACL) in networking?
A set of rules that permit or deny traffic based on criteria like IP, port, and protocol
Which criteria can a standard IPv4 ACL match on?
Source and destination IP, port, and protocol
Which criteria can an extended IPv4 ACL match on?
Source and destination IP, protocol, and port numbers
What is the implicit rule at the end of most ACLs?
An implicit deny that blocks traffic not explicitly permitted
Why does ACL rule order matter?
Rules are processed top to bottom, and the first match applies
Where should an extended ACL typically be placed for efficiency?
Close to the source of the traffic
Where is a standard ACL typically placed?
Which direction can an ACL be applied on an interface?
Allowing or blocking web access based on the requested URL or category
Which use case is BEST served by URL filtering?
Blocking access to malicious or inappropriate websites
Controlling access to content based on type, category, or keywords
Which device commonly performs URL and content filtering?
A proxy server or next-generation firewall
